In 1970, three astronauts were saved by a sock and some duct tape.
Two hundred thousand miles from Earth, an oxygen tank on Apollo 13 exploded.
The crew squeezed into their tiny lunar module and used it as a lifeboat.
But it was built for two people for two days. Now it had three, for four.
And every breath filled the cabin with more carbon dioxide.
The command module had spare air filters. But they were square, and the lunar module's holes were round.
So engineers on the ground dumped everything the crew had on board onto a table.
Plastic bags. Cardboard. Hoses. A sock. And duct tape.
They built a square filter that fit a round hole, and read the instructions up to space.
The crew built it, and the carbon dioxide started to fall.
Four days after the explosion, all three splashed down safely in the Pacific.
